newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Apr 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Apr 18.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO DAILY -- Guangdong authorities said at least 60,000 children in the province born of Hong Kong parents were qualified to move to the territory.
-- The first public meeting by Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa's office on proposed civil liberties legisltion was disrupted by a demonstration by pro-democracy activists.
-- SING TAO -- Beijing ordered all departments and related offices not to comment on renewed shipping links across the Taiwan Strait so there would be no fanfare and no media reports.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Beijing again urged the British authorities to cooperate on Hong Kong's transition, emphasising China had the ability to assure a smooth handover.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Future Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa has signalled that key terms in the proposed new Societies Ordinance could be redefined as long as it still prevented foreign political infiltration of the territory.
-- British officials in Vietnam are battling to stop a new flood of boatpeople leaving for Hong Kong, amid fears smugglers could be capitalising on uncertainties surrounding the handover.

-- HONG KONG STANDARD -- South Africa has further jeopardised the future status of its consulate-general in Hong Kong by recently opposing Beijing's move to block a discussion of China's human rights record at the United Nations.
